implementation: Added explicit SDK StateFormat metadata and bind_state_format() for callable state_dict/load_state_dict hooks, with exact FROM_VERSION->TO_VERSION migrator routes bound to declared entrypoints.

Worker validates finite JSON state against the declared schema before saving and before loading; same-version schema drift, missing identity, incompatible formats, downgrade and undeclared routes fail closed.

Checkpoint payload records callable module/source/distribution identity and a normalized environment inventory (distribution name/version/source kind, Python ABI, PyTorch/CUDA identity); no indexes or credentials are recorded.

Resume can exempt only one explicitly versioned state callable and its uniquely mapped owning distribution when an exact current migrator exists. Python/PyTorch identity, every other distribution, model/data/other training sources and source ownership remain exact. Ambiguous ownership, multiple state callables, missing inventories, unrelated changes and chained/mixed migrations are rejected.
Successful migrated external-loop resume loads the converted state and writes the next checkpoint in the current format. Checkpoint bytes are not rewritten during failed validation.

validation.result: passed: real CPU training created a v1 checkpoint, upgraded the extension callable/distribution, migrated state on resume, completed training, and saved a v2 checkpoint; an unrelated distribution change was rejected without modifying checkpoint bytes.
passed: 6 SDK manifest/schema tests, including exact callable migrator binding.
passed: 72 worker modules; embedded asset coverage and allowed import direction verified.

integration_points: The worker checkpoint code consumes the existing environment snapshot and source manifest; no Rust payload schema change was needed.
train.state imports extensions.metadata for the shared static state-schema validator. The architecture checker needs this explicit dependency edge; parent coordinator was notified and is handling it.
limitations: Versioned extension state must be finite JSON data and use the worker's supported object Schema subset; arbitrary Python values and tensor payloads are not portable under this contract.

Migration is one exact direct upgrade for one stateful callable/distribution. Multi-step migration chains, simultaneous callable migrations, mixed-format transitions, and package ownership ambiguities are deliberately unsupported.
Distribution inventory records normalized metadata, not artifact hashes or a reproducible lockfile. It proves exact reported versions/source categories, not wheel byte identity.
